Subject DR. S. G. HATEM
Made by D.S.I. Prokofiev Forwarded by D. S. J. Byrne

Shafick George HATEM arrived in Shanghai from Trieste
on September 5, 1933, in the s.s. "Conte Verde." From the
Aliens' Passport Declaration Form he filled up prior to dis-
embarkment it would appear that he is an American who was
born in 1910 at Buffalo, N.C. Giving his home address as
Roanoke Rapids, N.C., U.S.A., and his profession as doctor
of medicine, he travelled on U.S. passport No. 519 issued on
August 3, 1933, by the American Consulate-General at Geneva,
which bears a Chinese visa issued on August 11 of the same
year at Trieste. He stated that he intended to remain in
Shanghai for an indefinite period and that his object in
coming to this city was to practice medicine.

On September 11, 1933, Dr. Hatem, in company with Dr.
R.D. Levinson, applied for registration with the Shanghai
Medical Board. They presented doctor's diplomas of the
University of Geneva issued in 1933. After the local Consulate-
General for Switzerland had been communicated with regarding
the validity of their qualification papers, their applications
were approved and their names were included in the Shanghai
Municipal Council's register of medical practitioners for 1934.

On January 16, 1934, Dr. Hatem and Dr. Levinson
established their offices in Room 406, No. 10 Kiukiang Road
(Continental Bank Building) which they occupied until November
of the same year. Dr. Hatem's office address in 1935 was 39
Peking Road. Enquiries at Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.,
owners of the premises, show that Dr. Hatem's name never
appeared on the list of tenants and that, in all probability,
he shared an office with either Dr. E. G. Lebedevsky or Drs.
Ivy & Robinson in the same building. It will be recalled that

沙菲克·乔治·哈特姆（Shafick George HATEM）于1933年9月5日乘坐“绿伯爵号”（s.s. "Conte Verde"）轮船从的里雅斯特抵达上海。从他下船前填写的外侨护照申报单来看，他似乎是一名美国人，1910年出生于北卡罗来纳州布法罗（Buffalo, N.C.）。其家庭住址为美国北卡罗来纳州罗阿诺克拉皮兹（Roanoke Rapids, N.C., U.S.A.），职业为内科医生。他持有一本由美国驻日内瓦总领事馆于1933年8月3日签发的美国护照，号码为519号，该护照上有同年8月11日在的里雅斯特签发的中国签证。他声称打算在上海无限期停留，来此城市的目的是行医。

1933年9月11日，哈特姆医生与R.D. 莱文森（Levinson）医生一同向上海医务委员会申请注册。他们出示了1933年由日内瓦大学颁发的医学文凭。在与瑞士驻当地总领事馆就其资格证明文件的有效性进行沟通后，他们的申请获得批准，其名字被列入工部局1934年执业医师名册。

1934年1月16日，哈特姆医生和莱文森医生在九江路10号（大陆银行大楼）406室设立诊所，直至同年11月一直在此办公。1935年，哈特姆医生的诊所地址为北京路39号。向该物业业主怡和洋行有限公司（Jardine, Matheson & Co., Ltd.）查询显示，哈特姆医生的名字从未出现在租户名单上，而且极有可能他是与同一栋楼内的E. G. 列别杰夫斯基（Lebedevsky）医生或艾维（Ivy）与罗宾逊（Robinson）医生共用一间办公室。众所周知，

Morris Appelman (D.5180) upon his return in Shanghai from
Nagasaki on August 16, 1934, mentioned Dr. Hatem as a reference
in his Aliens' Passport Declaration Form. Further, it will
be recalled that Dr. Lobsovsky (died in 1935) who was an
official dentist to the staff of the local Soviet Consulate,
was also connected with Morris Appelman. It would, therefore,
appear that it was Dr. Lobsovsky with whom Dr. Hatem shared
an office at 39 Peking Road.
On April 26, 1934, Dr. Hatem applied at the S.M. Police
Traffic Office for a driving licence. On that occasion he gave
his address as No. 588 Yu Yuen Road and produced a note bearing
the signature of Mr. E. Farkas, Hungarian, who at that time
resided at No. 749 Yu Yuen Road, to the effect that he was
permitted to drive a motorcar owned by Mr. Farkas. On June 26,
1935, Dr. Hatem renewed his licence and gave his address as
Apt. 4, No. 260 Yu Yuen Road. He has not appeared at the
Traffic Office since that time and there is nothing on record
to show that he owns or uses a motor car.
In November, 1935, Dr. Hatem in reply to a communication
from the Public Health Department gave his office address as
Apartment 4, 260 Yu Yuen Road. He also intimated that Dr.
Levinson intended to leave Shanghai shortly.
At present it appears that Dr. Hatem is still residing at
the above address but that he does not receive patients there.
Reference to the available hong lists for 1934, 1935 and 1936
shows that Dr. Hatem's name is mentioned only in the hong list
for 1934. It does not appear in the telephone directory for
1936 (summer edition).

莫里斯·阿佩尔曼（Morris Appelman）（D.5180）于1934年8月16日从长崎返回上海时，在其外侨护照申报单中将哈特姆医生列为担保人。此外，众所周知，洛布索夫斯基（Lobsovsky）医生（1935年去世）是当地苏联领事馆工作人员的官方牙医，也与莫里斯·阿佩尔曼有联系。因此，看来与哈特姆医生在北京路39号共用办公室的是洛布索夫斯基医生。
1934年4月26日，哈特姆医生向工部局警务处交通股申请驾驶执照。当时他提供的地址是愚园路588号，并出示了一张带有匈牙利人E. 法卡斯（Farkas）先生签名的便条，法卡斯先生当时居住在愚园路749号，便条内容表明获准驾驶法卡斯先生拥有的一辆汽车。1935年6月26日，哈特姆医生更新了执照，提供的地址是愚园路260号4室。自那以后，他未再出现在交通股，记录中也没有任何迹象表明他拥有或使用汽车。
1935年11月，哈特姆医生在回复公共卫生处的函件时，提供的诊所地址为愚园路260号4室公寓。他还透露，莱文森医生打算不久后离开上海。
目前看来，哈特姆医生仍居住在上述地址，但他并不在那里接诊病人。查阅1934、1935和1936年的现有商行名录显示，哈特姆医生的名字仅出现在1934年的商行名录中。他的名字未出现在1936年（夏季版）电话簿中。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, MAY 2, 1936

VIRTUAL SLAVE
CONDITIONS IN
PLATING TRADE

Report Made by Medical
Association

WORKERS' HEALTH BAD

Metal Dust Causes Many
Complaints

SPECIAL TO THE "N.-C.D.N."

Conditions amounting to virtual slavery are revealed in the report of the Chinese Medical Association on the chromium plating and polishing industries in Shanghai. The report, drawn up by Dr. Bernard E. Read, Dr. S. G. Hatem, and Messrs. Dju Yǒ-bao and Lee Wei-yung, analyzes the living and working conditions of employees in the trade and shows that both are hopelessly inadequate.

The majority of the workers are between the ages of twelve and twenty years, according to the investigation; and far from being the benevolent and paternal system it is often represented to be, the apprentice system in this trade is shown to be heartless and cruel. Chinese law requires apprenticeship contracts but in actual fact these are seldom made. The report states:

Boys Farmed Out

"The apprenticeship system in China, of which this is an example, has often been described, but perhaps nowhere do its evils demonstrate themselves more clearly than in the trade now studied. There is a generally accepted view that the owner of a factory or workshop frequently takes into his service young lads who come from his own town of origin and are known to him, and that on this account he expresses a paternal interest in their whole well-being, even though they may have to work very hard. The present study has revealed that while this may be the case to some extent, a situation far otherwise exists concurrently. An entrepreneur, who may have paid a visit to a country district, will bring back a small boy, promising the parents that he will have him taught a trade. He goes from workshop to workshop, till finally he finds a master who is in need of another unpaid assistant. He hands the boy over and for this may receive a sum of some $8 for his services, and the new master may not even know his name or any facts concerning him. It is obvious that should he fall ill, or become injured there is little sense of responsibility on the part of the manager or owner of the workshop.

变相奴隶
状况

医学会提交的报告

工人健康状况恶劣

金属粉尘引发诸多
病症

《字林西报》特约专稿

中华医学会关于上海镀铬和抛光行业的报告揭示了相当于变相奴隶制的状况。该报告由伯纳德·E·里德（Bernard E. Read）医生、S. G. 哈特姆医生以及朱友宝（Dju Yǒ-bao，音译）和李维庸（Lee Wei-yung，音译）先生撰写，分析了该行业雇员的生活和工作条件，显示两者都严重不足。

调查显示，大多数工人的年龄在12至20岁之间；而且，这一行业的学徒制远非人们常描绘的那种仁慈和父权式的制度，而是显得无情和残酷。中国法律要求签订学徒合同，但实际上这些合同很少签订。报告指出：

被转卖的男孩

“中国的学徒制，以此为典型，虽常被描述，但或许 nowhere（无处）比在当前研究的行业中更清楚地显示出其弊端。普遍的观点认为，工厂或作坊的主人经常雇用来自其家乡且为他所知的年轻小伙子，并因此对他们的整体福祉表现出父亲般的关怀，尽管他们可能工作非常辛苦。本研究揭示，虽然情况在某种程度上可能如此，但同时存在的情况却大相径庭。一位企业家可能在访问农村地区后，带回一个小男孩，向父母承诺会教他一门手艺。他从一个作坊走到另一个作坊，直到最后找到一位需要另一名无薪助手的师傅。他将男孩交出去，并可能为此收取约8美元的服务费，而新师傅甚至可能不知道他的名字或有关他的任何事实。显然，如果男孩生病或受伤，经理或作坊主人几乎没有什么责任感。

dicate that some very casual relation-

turnover in other trades are avail-

age is sufficiently high within the

It is, however, known that when the

three or four years and is demanding

a younger unpaid boy in good health
fresh from the country."

Converted Dwelling Houses

Most of the chromium plating fac-
tories in Shanghai are converted
dwelling houses. They are usually
an ordinary Chinese house or shop,
containing one larger room and a
kitchen downstairs and two rooms
above. The front room, facing the
street, is usually adapted for buffing
and polishing, while the kitchen fre-
quently has plating vats installed.
The floor of the workshop is the
sleeping place of the apprentices
whose bedding by day may be seen
rolled up and placed in a corner of
the dusty polishing room. Lofts,
though the exit from them is pre-
carious in case of fire at night, are
nevertheless regarded as superior
sleeping accommodation and are
chosen by the older workers.
The conditions in the workshops
are often appalling. The hours of
work average out to eleven hours a
day. In polishing shops six or eight
buffing or polishing wheels are
crowded into as small a space as
possible. The older workers graduate
to wheels nearest the doorway where
there is more air and light. The
newest apprentice mans the wheels
farthest from the open air. He is
visible only dimly through the dense
cloud of dust which perpetually
arises from the wheels as the metal
is polished with the use of abrasives.
The dust never settles, for the shaft-
ing, being attached to the wooden
ceiling of a building not designed to
carry an industrial load, causes a
vibration which keeps the dust always
in motion.
The effect of these conditions upon
young workers can be imagined, and
the sickness rate among them is ex-
tremely high. The report referred to
gives details of the different diseases
found among the workers in the fac-
tories examined. Many of them are
directly attributable to the conditions
under which the youths have to earn
their keep. Nasal, respiratory and
lung complaints are common among
them, as can be understood when it
is realised that the atmosphere they
breathe for eleven hours of the day
is laden with metal dust and the
fumes of acids and other chemicals
used in the industry.
In the International Settlement it
is believed that more than 1,300 work-

或被解雇。这不能归因于任何经济萧条，因为每个地方的工人都得到了替换。由于在受医学检查的389名工人中，70%是20岁以下的少年，显而易见人员流动率很大，这表明存在某种非常随意的雇佣关系。没有其他行业的人员流动总体数据可供比较，但在短时间内百分比足够高，具有显著意义。也不清楚辞退工人是否与工人达到一定年龄和经验、从而必须为其服务支付报酬的情况相吻合。然而，众所周知，当男孩服满三四年学徒期并要求获得一些工资时，雇主往往觉得用一名刚从农村来的、身体健康的年轻无薪男孩替换他更为方便。”

改建的住宅

上海的大多数镀铬工厂都是由住宅改建而成的。它们通常是一栋普通的中国房屋或店铺，楼下有一个较大的房间和一个厨房，楼上有两个房间。面向街道的前厅通常被改造用于打磨和抛光，而厨房则经常安装电镀槽。车间的地面是学徒们的睡觉地方，白天可以看到他们的被褥卷起来放在布满灰尘的抛光室角落里。阁楼虽然夜间发生火灾时出口危险，但仍被视为较好的住宿条件，并被年长工人选用。
车间的条件往往令人震惊。工作时间平均每天十一小时。在抛光店中，六到八个打磨或抛光轮被尽可能拥挤地安置在狭小的空间内。年长工人逐渐移到靠近门口的轮子旁，那里空气和光线更多。最新的学徒操作离露天最远的轮子。在使用磨料抛光金属时，轮子不断扬起浓密的灰尘云，只能隐约看到他。灰尘从不沉降，因为传动轴附着在未设计承受工业负荷的建筑物的木质天花板上，引起振动，使灰尘始终处于运动状态。
可以想象这些条件对年轻工人的影响，他们的患病率极高。前述报告详细列举了在受检工厂工人中发现的各种疾病。其中许多直接归因于青年们赖以谋生的条件。鼻部、呼吸道和肺部疾病在他们中间很常见，这是因为人们意识到，他们每天呼吸十一小时的空气中充满了金属粉尘以及该行业使用的酸和其他化学物质的烟雾。
